### ① Derived judgments

The card's three defects and the PR's claims, one at a time:

1. File surface. The PR is one commit (478c92a0, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, head repo = base repo, draft, base `main`); `git diff 04e0c2c0 478c92a0 --stat`, the REST file listing and `changed_files: 2` agree on exactly scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs (+59/−10, blob 07d17a67f3) and scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs (+129/−22, blob ae829bc186). The claim's file surface was the two files and their self-tests (the self-tests live inside the files); no other path is touched. Neither file moved on origin/main since the merge-base. Correct, and on surface.
2. Defect ① — a GitHub 403 inside the relay runner read as the egress proxy's. `stopSignalFrom` and `noteResponse` now act on `proxyAnswered(body, env)`, which is `!inActionsRunner(env) && isProxyRefusal(body)`, with `inActionsRunner` reading `env.GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`. In `noteResponse` the env is `deps.env ?? process.env`; on the live path `main()` calls `executeFleetWrite` with no `pace` deps, so `rest()` passes `paceDeps = {}` and `noteResponse` reads `process.env`, which the Actions runner populates. So on the runner every answer is judged by rule ③: a 403 with a back-off signal writes the marker, a bare 403 keeps its slot spent, writes no marker, releases the lease and prints no proxy line; the slot give-back and the "No stop marker written" line are unreachable there. Measured: the self-test's runner harness case (plain 403, then a proxy-shaped 403 carrying a ratelimit verdict) passes, and ablation W1 (`proxyAnswered` ignoring the runner) reds 3 of 118, W3 (`stopSignalFrom` back to body-only) reds 2, W4 (`noteResponse` back to body-only) reds 1, each naming the runner cases. Fixed, and covered.
3. Defect ① second half — `isProxyRefusal` needs a positive mark. The body-only predicate now returns true on the proxy's own message or on a `documentation_url` matching `PROXY_DOC_HOSTS` (anthropic.com, claude.com, claude.ai and subdomains, anchored on the host); "not on github.com" no longer counts. The measured proxy shape (message naming the proxy, docs URL on the proxy's own host) still reads true, so the seat-side path is unchanged for the real proxy. Ablation W2 (the old off-github test restored) reds 2 of 118 (the short-link/changelog/look-alike-host case and the `proxyAnswered` case). Correct. `PROXY_DOC_HOSTS` is declared after `isProxyRefusal`, which only reads it at call time; no temporal-dead-zone risk.
4. Seat-side proxy path still works (outside the runner). `label-write.mjs` `classifyHttp` keeps `isProxyRefusal(body)` → `prerequisite`, and `fleet-token.mjs` keeps `isProxyRefusal(minted)` for its sentence; both are pure body reads and both are true on the measured proxy shape. In a seat container (`GITHUB_ACTIONS` unset) `noteResponse` still gives the slot back on a proxy refusal (the existing `proxy-refusal.jsonl` harness case, now with `env: {}`, passes). The one behaviour change seat-side is deliberate: a GitHub 403 whose docs URL is off github.com is now classified by status (`refusal`, or `ratelimit` with a zero header) rather than `prerequisite`. `label-write` 136/11 and `fleet-token` 75/8 self-tests are green on the head. Correct.
5. Defect ② — the refusal prints the platform's message and `documentation_url`, never the payload. `advisoryRefusalCause(answer, known)` reads `answer.detail` (which `rest()` derives from `json.message` alone, token-scrubbed) or `json.message`, flattens control characters, whitespace, `|`, backtick and `"`, caps at 200 with a note, and prints `documentation_url` only when https-shaped (`REFUSAL_URL_SHAPE`, no quotes, spaces, pipes or angle brackets) and at most 200 characters; the `errors` array and the rest of the body are never read. The `known` set is `advisoryProseOf` of the request body and, for the PATCH rows, of the advisory the preflight read (`pre.known`); ids, states, logins and URL-shaped words are excluded, strings under 8 characters too. A message, or a URL (raw or percent-decoded), reproducing any 16-character run of a known string is withheld and the row says so. Reached from `confirmAdvisory` (report, draft, PATCH) and from `advisoryPreflight`'s refused GET; `advisoryPlatformText` is no longer imported by execute.mjs. Measured: ablation E1 (`quotesKnown` → false) reds 5 of 240 including the marker sweep; E2 (cause hidden) reds 8; E3 (no cap) reds 1; E4 (URL printed unshaped, including a `javascript:` URL and an over-long one) reds 1; E5 (`pre.known` dropped) reds 2 including the marker sweep; E6 (preflight refusal without cause) reds 1. The marker sweep covers 45 runs (41 before) and finds the marker in no log line, row, summary, annotation or pace-log line; the positive controls still hold. Fixed, and covered on every path.
6. Leak surface, read against the code rather than the tests. The only new text any advisory row emits is `advisoryRefusalCause`'s return, composed of fixed prose, the flattened/capped `message` and a shape-checked `documentation_url`. `message` is the platform's own field; the `errors` array (the one field GitHub does fill with submitted values on a 422) is never touched; the request body and the preflight's advisory reach the function only as the `known` blocklist. `detail` is token-scrubbed in `rest()` before it reaches the cause; the URL is not scrubbed, but it is platform-authored, shape-checked and never carries the bearer token. Annotations are emitted only for landed report/draft rows (`::notice` with the id), never for a failed row. No path prints a `summary`, `description`, vulnerability, credit or any secret into a log line, row, summary or annotation. Two robustness gaps, neither a leak today, are should-fixes S2 and S3 below.
7. Defect ③ — the row's advice names the cause. Every refused advisory row now reads `FAILED: HTTP <status>; cause, as the platform gives it: "<message>" (documentation: <url>); <ADVISORY_ACCESS_REMEDY>`, or the withheld/unread variants, and the same text reaches the step summary and the log (the unlisted-message case asserts all three). The six-string filter that hid the measured 403's message is gone from these two paths. Fixed.
8. The PR body against the head. 118/12 with rule ③ 14 → 19 (diff: the battery row and five new cases); 240/21 with the advisory battery 27 → 30 (diff) and the sweep 41 → 45 (diff); both ablation readings (5 of 240 for `quotesKnown`, 3 of 118 for `proxyAnswered`) reproduce exactly; 36 derived commands (measured 36); `skip-changeset` is right (scripts/pm publishes nothing; Check Changeset success); `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right (no published schema, no authorable surface). Every body claim checked holds. One body matter is S1.
9. Gates. Of the 36 derived commands, 16 were run here: `check:pm-fleet-write-validate` (275/15), `check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch` (dispatch and rerun-failed, exit 0), `check:scripts-symbol-anchors` (4155 anchors resolve, so removing the `advisoryPlatformText` import broke no anchor), `check:nul-bytes`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:parse-guard`, `check-self-test-wired` (run and `--self-test`), `check:pm-dispatch-gates` (254 s), `check:watch-hint-literal`, `check:agent-test-spelling`, `check:ratchet-remedy-authority`, `check:gitlink-declared`, `check-declaration-mirrors`, all exit 0. Two did not exit 0 for reasons outside the diff: `check:doc-authoring` (rc 3, pnpm refusing to run without node_modules in the throwaway worktree) and `check-self-test-workflow-commands` (rc 1, `release-pending-publish.mjs` cannot find `@changesets/cli` without node_modules; the finding names neither file). CI's `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are success on the head, which covers both. ESLint was not run locally for the same reason; CI's is the reading.
10. Nothing new on any surface: no gate, label, workflow, CODEOWNERS, package or governed-register path. The fixtures name no real advisory: the ids are made-up shapes, the marker is a generic sentence, the unlisted message is invented, and the CWE values are category ids, not advisories. The card, the PR body and the dev report carry no finding and no mechanism.

### ② Semver level

None. No published package, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no TypeScript; scripts/pm tooling only. `skip-changeset` is the right declaration and Check Changeset is success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: none.
- Dev out-of-scope note (a): ops.mjs's header (lines 433 to 434) still says the platform's `message` is printed only when `ADVISORY_PLATFORM_MESSAGES` names it, and `ADVISORY_ACCESS_REMEDY` still says what the App may do "is decided by the first live run" (that run has happened: one 201 then 403s). After this PR `ADVISORY_PLATFORM_MESSAGES` and `advisoryPlatformText` have no production caller (validate.mjs's self-test alone). label-write.mjs line 420 likewise still describes the proxy mark as "a `documentation_url` that is not GitHub's". Judgment: follow-ups, not blockers. The file that does the printing (execute.mjs) carries the correct header; the drift is in neighbouring files the claim held outside the surface, and it describes old behaviour rather than enabling a wrong one. Folded into S1's follow-up card.
- Dev out-of-scope note (b): a bare 403 on the runner writes no stop marker under rule ③. Judgment: follow-up, not a blocker. Rule ③'s own text says a plain 403 writes none; the card's "takes the platform back-off path" is met in that rule ③ now judges the answer. The runner's pace log is per-run, so a marker there would not stop a second seat anyway; stopping repeat sends is seat-side, and belongs with the rest-channel.md rule the card's third bullet asks for after the live reading (S1). Whether rule ③ should read a documented daily-limit message as a back-off signal is a design question for after that reading, since the body is still unread.
- `execute.mjs` is also edited on #29420's branch (not yet pushed; no `origin` head names 29420). The dev's note (whichever lands second merges main, the seat re-reviews the delta) is the right handling.
- Independence: PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, commit author Claude; no off-relay author note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

Per hits file, against the card's scenario (a second `advisory_report` of the day refused by GitHub inside the relay runner, read by a seat that must decide whether to stop):

- `scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs`: splitting "could a proxy be in the path" (`proxyAnswered`, env) from "does this body read as the proxy's" (`isProxyRefusal`, pure) is the right cut: the body predicate stays shared with the seat-side transports unchanged in signature, the env predicate is the one thing that differs between a runner and a seat, and `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is the documented default variable for exactly that question. Requiring a positive mark closes the misreading the card measured without loosening the proxy case. The `env` threading (`stopSignalFrom` field, `noteResponse` `deps.env`) is minimal and defaulted. Holds.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`: printing the platform's `message` and docs URL under caps, shape checks and a prose-quote blocklist is a sound replacement for a six-string allowlist: the allowlist's failure mode was the card's defect ② (an unlisted message hides the cause), while the blocklist's failure mode is a withheld cause with a line saying so. Excluding ids, logins, states and URL-shaped words from `known` is reasoned correctly (an advisory's own `url` shares its path with GitHub's docs). Keeping `errors` out entirely is right: it is the one field that echoes submitted values. The two should-fixes below tighten the guard's robustness; the design holds.

Must-fix: none.

Should-fix:
- S1 (PR body, seat's call before landing, no new head): the body says `Fixes #29402`, but the card's third Expected bullet (the seat reads the actual reason once and records it with its seat-side rule in `references/rest-channel.md`) is deliberately left out of this PR, and the dev report carries it as "noted, not filed". Under review-checklist's Fixes/Part-of rule, either switch to `Part of #29402` and arrange the close in a comment, or file the follow-up card and name it in the body. The same card should carry the out-of-surface drift from ③: ops.mjs header lines 433 to 434 and `ADVISORY_ACCESS_REMEDY`'s "first live run", the now-callerless `ADVISORY_PLATFORM_MESSAGES`/`advisoryPlatformText`, label-write.mjs line 420, and the bare-403 seat-side stop rule.
- S2 (execute.mjs, one line): `quotesKnown(oneLine, known)` compares the flattened message with unflattened known prose, so a quoted fragment that straddles a `|`, backtick or `"` in the known text matches only if one side alone spans 16 characters. Add `quotesKnown(raw, known)` beside it (or flatten `known` the same way). Not a leak today: GitHub's refusal `message` does not echo submitted prose, the `errors` array that does is never printed, and the marker sweep is green.
- S3 (execute.mjs, cosmetic): on `status: 0` (fetch threw) `rest()` puts the transport error's text in `detail`, and the row then says "cause, as the platform gives it: ..." for text the platform never sent. Branch on `status === 0` to say the request did not reach the platform.
